result.question: What does Tesla disclose about its dependence on Elon Musk?
result.answer:
Tesla discloses in its SEC filings that it is "highly dependent on the services of Elon Musk, Technoking of Tesla and our Chief Executive Officer" [0001628280-26-003952:item-1a-p016]. The company states that none of its key employees, including Musk, is bound by an employment agreement for any specific term, and it may not be able to successfully attract and retain senior leadership necessary to grow its business [0001628280-26-003952:item-1a-p016].

Tesla further discloses that although Mr. Musk spends significant time with Tesla and is highly active in its management, he does not devote his full time and attention to Tesla [0001628280-26-003952:item-1a-p017]. In its most recent 10-K (filed January 29, 2026), Tesla notes that Mr. Musk also currently holds management positions at Space Exploration Technologies Corp., X.AI Holdings Corp. ("xAI"), Neuralink Corp. and The Boring Company, and is involved in other ventures [0001628280-26-003952:item-1a-p017]. The prior year's 10-K (filed January 30, 2025) had additionally listed X Corp. and involvement with the Department of Government Efficiency among his other commitments [0001628280-25-003063:item-1a-p016].

Tesla also warns that if Elon Musk were forced to sell shares of its common stock, either that he has the ability to pledge to secure certain personal loan obligations or in satisfaction of other obligations, such sales could cause Tesla's stock price to decline [0001628280-26-003952:item-1a-p034]. Certain banking institutions have in the past made extensions of credit to Mr. Musk that were secured by pledges of Tesla common stock, and if the stock price were to decline substantially, he may be forced to sell shares to satisfy loan obligations [0001628280-26-003952:item-1a-p035]. Mr. Musk may also sell shares to satisfy tax obligations relating to the 2018 CEO Performance Award or to fund investments in significant business or other ventures [0001628280-26-003952:item-1a-p035].

Additionally, Tesla discloses a risk that the technologies and initiatives associated with the 2025 CEO Performance Award, including the product goals, may be misaligned with current or future consumer demand [0001628280-26-003952:item-1a-p034]. The product goals were designed to incentivize Elon Musk to devote time and energy to development of these products and services, as these products and services are directionally consistent with Mr. Musk's vision for the future of the company [0001628280-26-003952:item-1a-p034].
